test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 10 Feb 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: P, Q and R participated in a cycle race of 4000 metres. P cycles twice as fast as Q and R cycles 1over2 as fast as Q. If R completes the race in 40 minutes, then what is the speed (in km/h) of P?
solution:
**Formula:**

S = D over T, where

D = Distance

S = Speed

T = Time 

**Concept:**

Speed and Time are inversely proportional. This means that if the speed is more, time required will be less and vice-versa.

**Calculation:**

According to the question-

R cycles 1over2 as fast as Q and requires 40 minutes to complete the race

⇒ Q requires 20 min to complete the race.

P cycles twice as fast as Q

⇒ P requires 10 min i.e., half as much timing as Q.

Total time taken by P in seconds = 10 × 60 = 600 sec

Speed of P = 4000over 600 = 20over3 m/s

Speed of P in km/h = 20over3 × 18over5 = 24 km/h

∴ **The speed of P is 24 km/h.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] __Additional Information__** To convert m/s into km/h, we multiply by 18over5 . Conversely, to convert km/h to m/s, we multiply by 5over18.
